visuals.at: Strong answer: usually three things at once
visuals.title: How a buyout goes wrong

items.label: Cash flow falls
items.detail: Competition, a downturn or a change in how customers buy

items.label: The debt doesn't
items.detail: Sized for the old cash flow, so leverage jumps and interest cover collapses

items.label: A deadline
items.detail: A covenant test, or a maturity nobody will refinance

items.label: The buyout breaks
items.detail: Take away any one of the three and a deal usually survives

visuals.at: Then the options, from mildest to hardest
visuals.title: Facing a covenant breach: the sponsor's options

items.label: Waiver or amendment
items.detail: Lenders reset the test, for a fee and usually a higher interest rate

items.label: Equity cure
items.detail: The sponsor puts in new equity, which repays debt or counts towards EBITDA

items.label: Asset sales
items.detail: Sell parts of the business to repay debt

items.label: Restructuring
items.detail: The fulcrum creditors swap debt for equity; the sponsor usually loses the company

visuals.title: Quiz
visuals.text: Five questions. Answer along on the cards below the transcript, then hear Marco's answers.

quiz.pause_at: Pause here if you want to think it through

questions.q: Harbour has £600m of debt and its EBITDA falls from £100m to £70m. What's its leverage now?
questions.explain: Leverage is debt over EBITDA: 600 ÷ 70 ≈ 8.6x, up from 6x at entry. The debt doesn't shrink when EBITDA does.
questions.explain_at: six hundred over seventy, about eight point six times

questions.q: Harbour's EBITDA falls to £70m and buyers still pay 10x. With £600m of debt, what is the fund's £400m of equity now worth?
questions.explain: 10 × 70 = 700, minus 600 of debt = 100: EBITDA fell 30%, the equity 75%. Sofia's 280 assumes the equity falls in line with EBITDA.
questions.explain_at: Take off six hundred of debt and the equity is one hundred

questions.q: What did Toys R Us aim to do when it filed for Chapter 11 in September 2017?

options.text: Close its stores and sell the stock
Float the company on the market again
Hand the company to its suppliers

questions.explain: Chapter 11 is a court process for reorganising a company. Toys R Us planned to borrow $2bn to pay suppliers for Christmas; liquidation came six months later.
questions.explain_at: Chapter Eleven is the American court process for reorganising a company

questions.q: A sponsor puts new equity into a portfolio company to bring it back inside its covenant. What's that called?
questions.explain: In an equity cure the sponsor's new money repays debt or counts towards EBITDA for the test. A waiver comes from the lenders; a debt-for-equity swap is a restructuring.
questions.explain_at: An equity cure: the sponsor puts in new equity

questions.q: Mobico's shares are valued at about £308m and its enterprise value at about £2.3bn. What fills the gap?

options.text: The premium over the share price
Debt, the hybrid and other claims

questions.explain: The bridge of about £2bn is net debt of £1,134m, the £500m hybrid, £285m of provisions and £97m of other items such as pensions. The equity is a thin slice on top.
